# Build your foundations

[← Main guide](../README.md) · [Browse resources](resources.md)

Start with the skills your first project needs. You can learn the deeper mathematics alongside your work; completing every course here is not an entry requirement.

## Python, R, and the command line

**Level:** Beginner

Choose a language for a concrete task, then learn to read, transform, and visualize a small dataset.

**Before you begin:** No programming experience required.

### What to understand

- Python: variables, functions, tables, plotting, and small scripts.
- R: data frames, factors, tidy data, plotting, and biological analysis packages.
- Shell: paths, pipes, redirection, permissions, and inspecting a text file.

### What you’ll be able to do

Write a short script that reads a table, checks its columns, and saves a useful summary.

### Try this

Use one small table in either Python or R. Report missing values, summarize one measurement by group, and plot the result. Explain the biological meaning of each column.

### Keep in mind

Choose one language for your first project. Language preference depends on the analysis and team; you do not need to learn Python and R simultaneously.

### A few good resources

- [The Python Tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/) — Documentation · Beginner · Free · English. The official language tutorial. Use it as a reference while writing small scripts rather than reading everything before practicing.
  - Prerequisites: Some general programming familiarity; complete beginners can start with a guided lesson.

- [R for Data Science, second edition](https://r4ds.hadley.nz/) — Book · Beginner · Free online · English. A practical route through importing, transforming, visualizing, and communicating tabular data in R.
  - Prerequisites: No prior R experience.

- [Data Carpentry: genomics lessons](https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/#genomics) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Learn project organization, the command line, sequence processing, and computing through biological examples.
  - Prerequisites: No prior command-line experience for the introductory lessons.

- [Elzero: Mastering Python](https://elzero.org/category/courses/mastering-python/) — Course · Beginner · Free · Arabic. An Arabic-language programming entry point retained from the original resource list. Pair the lessons with a small biological data task.
  - Prerequisites: No prior Python experience.

<a id="biological-data"></a>

## Biological data and file formats

**Level:** Beginner

Understand what a file represents before choosing a tool to process it.

**Before you begin:** Basic molecular biology and the ability to inspect a text file.

### What to understand

- Sequences and reads: FASTA, FASTQ, quality scores, and reference versions.
- Alignments and annotation: SAM/BAM, VCF, BED, and GTF/GFF; learn coordinate conventions explicitly.
- Analysis objects: count matrices, sample metadata, AnnData, and MuData.
- Structures: PDB and mmCIF, chains, residues, assemblies, and identifiers.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain the inputs, outputs, identifiers, and coordinate system of your chosen analysis.

### Try this

Make a data dictionary for a tutorial dataset. Record its accession, organism, reference genome or structure, sample units, and file formats.

### Keep in mind

Gene symbols, stable identifiers, and reference builds are not interchangeable. Preserve the versions and mapping decisions used in your analysis.

### A few good resources

- [Data Carpentry: genomics lessons](https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/#genomics) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Learn project organization, the command line, sequence processing, and computing through biological examples.
  - Prerequisites: No prior command-line experience for the introductory lessons.

- [Ensembl training](https://training.ensembl.org/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Learn to navigate genome annotation, identifiers, comparative data, and Ensembl tools using worked training materials.
  - Prerequisites: Basic genetics.

- [NCBI Learn](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/learn/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Find official introductions and training for NCBI databases and tools; choose a tutorial that matches your data source.
  - Prerequisites: Basic molecular biology.

- [AnnData documentation](https://anndata.readthedocs.io/en/stable/) — Documentation · Intermediate · Free · English. Understand the annotated matrix structure used in many Python single-cell workflows, including observations, variables, and layers.
  - Prerequisites: Python and basic single-cell matrices.

- [PDB-101: understanding PDB data](https://pdb101.rcsb.org/learn/guide-to-understanding-pdb-data/introduction) — Guide · Beginner · Free · English. A welcoming introduction to structure files, experimental information, assemblies, and interpretation.
  - Prerequisites: Basic protein biology.

<a id="statistics"></a>

## Statistics and experimental design

**Level:** Beginner

Connect statistical decisions to the biological question and experimental units.

**Before you begin:** Basic tables and plots; learn probability concepts as needed.

### What to understand

- Biological versus technical replication, controls, randomization, and confounding.
- Distributions, effect sizes, uncertainty, hypothesis tests, and multiple testing.
- Linear models, covariates, batch effects, and exploratory data analysis.
- For single-cell studies, identify the independent biological samples before testing.

### What you’ll be able to do

Describe the comparison, independent samples, covariates, and limitations of a small study.

### Try this

Sketch two experimental designs: one where treatment is confounded with batch, and one where it is balanced. Explain what can be learned from each.

### Keep in mind

A small adjusted p-value does not establish a large effect or causality. Interpret effect sizes, design, and uncertainty together.

### A few good resources

- [Statistical Thinking for the 21st Century](https://statsthinking21.github.io/statsthinking21-core-site/) — Book · Beginner · Free online · English. Develop statistical reasoning about data, probability, inference, and models before relying on a test by name.
  - Prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and willingness to work through examples.

- [Bioconductor: gene-level RNA-seq workflow](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/workflows/html/rnaseqGene.html) — Workflow · Intermediate · Free · English. Connect RNA-seq processing with exploratory analysis and differential expression through a documented workflow.
  - Prerequisites: Basic R, sample metadata, and introductory statistics.

- [Single-cell Best Practices](https://www.sc-best-practices.org/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.
  - Prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.

<a id="reproducibility"></a>

## Git, environments, and research habits

**Level:** Beginner

Make it possible for your future self and a collaborator to repeat your work.

**Before you begin:** A small script or notebook.

### What to understand

- Git commits, branches, readable READMEs, and reviewable changes.
- Separate input data, code, configuration, and generated results.
- Record package versions, random seeds, parameters, and dataset accessions.
- Use environments first; learn containers when your workflow needs portability.

### What you’ll be able to do

Share a small project with clear setup and rerun instructions.

### Try this

Ask a peer to reproduce one plot using only your README. Record any missing dependency, parameter, or data-download instruction and repair it.

### Keep in mind

A notebook that ran once is not sufficient documentation. Restart the session and rerun it from the beginning before sharing.

### A few good resources

- [Software Carpentry: Version Control with Git](https://swcarpentry.github.io/git-novice/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Practice tracking changes, working with remote repositories, and collaborating on a small project.
  - Prerequisites: Basic command-line use.

- [Data Carpentry: genomics lessons](https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/#genomics) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Learn project organization, the command line, sequence processing, and computing through biological examples.
  - Prerequisites: No prior command-line experience for the introductory lessons.

- [Conda: managing environments](https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/tasks/manage-environments.html) — Documentation · Beginner · Free · English. Create and document isolated software environments, including environment files that can be shared with collaborators.
  - Prerequisites: Basic command-line use.

- [Quarto: getting started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Combine analysis, narrative, and outputs in a reproducible report rather than copying results into an unrelated document.
  - Prerequisites: Basic R or Python for executable examples.

<a id="math"></a>

## Mathematics when you need it

**Level:** Intermediate

Build intuition for the mathematics behind the methods you actually use.

**Before you begin:** School-level algebra; programming helps with experiments.

### What to understand

- Linear algebra: vectors, matrices, projections, eigenvectors, and PCA.
- Probability: conditional probability, likelihood, and uncertainty.
- Calculus and optimization: gradients, objectives, and iterative fitting.

### What you’ll be able to do

Explain one method's inputs, objective, assumptions, and outputs in plain language.

### Try this

Apply PCA to a small numeric table, then explain what the axes describe and how scaling changes the result.

### Keep in mind

These topics are deeper study options. Do not delay an accessible first project until you have completed all of them.

### A few good resources

- [MIT OpenCourseWare: Linear Algebra](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-06-linear-algebra-spring-2010/) — Course · Intermediate · Free · English. A deeper route into matrices, projections, and related concepts that support PCA and machine learning.
  - Prerequisites: Algebra; consult the course's own prerequisite guidance.

- [Statistical Thinking for the 21st Century](https://statsthinking21.github.io/statsthinking21-core-site/) — Book · Beginner · Free online · English. Develop statistical reasoning about data, probability, inference, and models before relying on a test by name.
  - Prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and willingness to work through examples.

- [Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.ai/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. Build conceptual and practical foundations in deep learning; select chapters relevant to the model you are studying.
  - Prerequisites: Python, probability, linear algebra, and basic calculus for deeper chapters.
